title: El Niño and India's Rain

endcard.line: Footage: Mostafameraji (CC0). Picture: Andrew Cattoir, US National Park Service (public domain)

segments.say: Thousands of kilometres away, in the Pacific Ocean, a patch of sea warms up by a degree or two. And farmers in India start to worry.

anim.title: A normal year
items: Trade winds blow west across the Pacific
Warm water piles up near Asia
Air rises there and brings rain

segments.say: In a normal year, trade winds push warm surface water west across the Pacific. Warm, moist air rises over that water and brings rain.

anim.title: An El Niño year
items: Warm water spreads east, towards South America

segments.say: In an El Niño year, the trade winds weaken. The warm water spreads east, towards South America, and the rising air moves with it.
Over India, more air sinks instead of rising. So the monsoon is often weaker, and droughts become more likely.
But not always. In nineteen ninety-seven, a very strong El Niño came, and India's monsoon was still normal. The Indian Ocean had its own say.
Its opposite is La Niña, when the eastern Pacific turns cooler than usual. La Niña years often bring India a good monsoon. The swing comes every two to seven years.
For GS One: El Niño warms the eastern Pacific, weakens the trade winds, and often, but not always, weakens India's monsoon.

sources: NCERT Class 11, India: Physical Environment, ch. 4 (Climate): El Niño, warm current off Peru, linked to weaker Indian monsoon; used in long-range forecasts
NOAA Climate.gov, 'What is the El Niño–Southern Oscillation (ENSO) in a nutshell?': trade winds weaken in El Niño, warm water shifts east; La Niña is the cool phase; episodes recur every 2–7 years
IMD, Monsoon Report 1997: all-India June–September rainfall was 102% of the long-period average despite a strong El Niño; positive Indian Ocean Dipole cited

quiz.q: What happens to the Pacific trade winds in an El Niño year?
quiz.why: Weaker trade winds let the warm water spread east.

quiz.q: Why does El Niño often weaken India's monsoon?
options: It cools the Bay of Bengal
More air sinks over India instead of rising
quiz.why: With the rising air shifted east, more air sinks over India, so less rain.

options: A strong El Niño can still come with a normal monsoon
La Niña causes floods every year
quiz.why: 1997 had a very strong El Niño but a normal monsoon.

reviewNote: Facts were read against NCERT's climate chapter, NOAA's ENSO explainer and IMD's 1997 monsoon figures. Diagrams are schematic, no map. Moving facts: none; the El Niño–monsoon link is a tendency, stated as one.
